Here’s a quick‑look table of the **long‑weekend holidays** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(Only holidays that fell on a Monday or Friday—or were observed on a Monday when they landed on a weekend—created a true “extended” weekend.)

| Holiday | Calendar Date (2023) | Observed (if applicable) | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|----------------------|--------------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | Monday Jan 2 | **Jan 1–3** |
| Family Day (BC, AB, ON, SK, NB, PE) | Monday Feb 20 | – | **Feb 18–20** |
| Good Friday | Friday Apr 7 | – | **Apr 7–9** |
| Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | – | **May 20–22** |
| Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 | Monday Jul 3 | **Jul 1–3** |
| Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | – | **Sep 2–4** |
| Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | – | **Oct 7–9** |
| Remembrance Day | Saturday Nov 11 | Monday Nov 13 | **Nov 11–13** |
| Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | – | **Dec 23–25** |

> **Note:**  
> • Boxing Day (Dec 26 2023) fell on a Tuesday, so it didn’t create a long weekend.  
> • Provincial holidays that didn’t land on a Monday/Friday (e.g., Heritage Day in Alberta, St. Patricks’ Day in Ontario) also didn’t form long weekends.

Feel free to plug these dates straight into your holiday‑planning app!
